name: Sony PlayStation 4 family
summary: Explore PS4 family hardware and firmware-specific routes into homebrew across the original, Slim and Pro models.

specs.cpu: AMD semi-custom x86-64 APU; die marks differ by model group
specs.gpu: AMD Radeon-based GPU; 4K output on Pro only
specs.storage: Internal 2.5-inch SATA hard drive, 500 GB on launch models; user-replaceable
specs.media: Blu-ray drive on all models; no UHD Blu-ray on any PS4

variants.storage: 500 GB HDD on launch models; larger options followed
variants.notes: CUH-10xx, CUH-11xx and CUH-12xx model groups. Launch model with a glossy/split case; no HDR at launch.

variants.storage: 500 GB or 1 TB HDD depending on SKU
variants.notes: CUH-20xx, CUH-21xx and CUH-22xx model groups. Smaller case with no optical audio port.

specs.cpu: AMD semi-custom x86-64 APU (Belize / Belize2 southbridge)

variants.notes: CUH-70xx, CUH-71xx and CUH-72xx model groups. Mid-generation performance model; later 72xx SKUs use the Baikal southbridge.

specs.cpu: AMD semi-custom x86-64 APU (Belize2 / Baikal southbridge)

homebrew.name: PPPwn
homebrew.firmware: Kernel RCE for PS4 up to FW 11.00 with an exact supported-version list. The README says it only prints PPPwned and that enabler payloads must be adapted separately.
homebrew.summary: A PC-driven PPPoE kernel exploit entry point for PS4. It runs from a computer with an Ethernet port and only covers the firmware revisions listed below.

compatibility.note: These exact revisions are listed upstream. No separate model-specific list is published; southbridge differences matter for later payloads rather than for this entry exploit.

requirements: PS4 on one of the listed firmware revisions.
A PC with an Ethernet port (a USB Ethernet adapter works) and a PPPoE connection configured on the console.
An adapted payload such as GoldHEN or another homebrew enabler; PPPwn itself only prints PPPwned.
warnings: Updating past 11.00 removes this route; Sony provides no official downgrade.
Online use of a modified console risks an account or console ban.
Third-party payloads can crash the console.

homebrew.name: GoldHEN
homebrew.firmware: Upstream publishes no supported-firmware list; the PPPwn entry-exploit list is the practical boundary.
homebrew.summary: The homebrew enabler payload for PS4. It provides plugins, rest-mode support, external HDD support, internal pkg installation, debug settings and servers, among other features.

compatibility.note: GoldHEN's README documents features and warns about third-party payloads, but publishes no firmware matrix. Compatibility follows the entry exploit used to load it.

requirements: A working PS4 entry exploit and payload loader.
GoldHEN payload matching the console's firmware and model group.
warnings: GoldHEN's README warns that third-party payloads can be harmful or crash the console.
Source code is not public; keep payloads to upstream releases.
Rest Mode may need USB power for payloads that must survive a resume.

homebrew.name: PS4 Linux (ps4-linux-loader)
homebrew.firmware: kexec Linux payloads for FW 5.05 through 13.52 across Aeolia, Belize/Belize2 and Baikal; FW 14.00 is marked with a question mark upstream.
homebrew.summary: kexec-based Linux payloads for PS4. The host works with GoldHEN's PayLoader and boots a separate Linux kernel from /data/linux/boot or a USB drive.

compatibility.note: These exact revisions are listed upstream. A payload still needs a working entry exploit first, so the practical ceiling is the lower of the exploit and Linux lists.
Upstream marks FW 14.00 with a question mark; not confirmed as working.

requirements: A working entry exploit and GoldHEN's PayLoader.
Linux kernel (bzImage) and initramfs.cpio.gz placed in /data/linux/boot or /user/system/boot, or on a USB drive.
A PS4 model whose southbridge is covered (Aeolia, Belize/Belize2 or Baikal).
warnings: Linux is not the console OS; PS4 games do not run under it.
A 13.00 console appears in the Linux list but not in PPPwn's supported versions.
A black screen can result from an outdated kernel; use an up-to-date guide.
Updating past a supported firmware removes the entry exploit even if a Linux payload exists.

homebrew.name: Sony PS4 system software update and reinstall
homebrew.firmware: Latest official system software: 14.00. Update and reinstallation files are different.
homebrew.summary: Sony's official instructions for updating a PS4 from USB or reinstalling system software in Safe Mode. Reinstalling erases console data and does not provide an older-firmware selector.

compatibility.note: Official PS4 recovery and update track shared by the whole family; reinstall does not accept older firmware.

requirements: FAT32- or exFAT-formatted USB drive with the PS4 update file in the documented folder; use Safe Mode as Sony documents.
warnings: Sony's Safe Mode reinstall deletes all PS4 data.
Update and reinstallation PUPs are different files and are not interchangeable.
Reinstalling does not downgrade the console.

homebrew.name: PS4 firmware rollback status — no verified general method
homebrew.firmware: No general rollback firmware support established
homebrew.summary: Records the documented PS4 downgrade limit: Sony's tools are forward-only and no general rollback method is documented. This is a status reference, not a downgrade tool.

compatibility.note: No PS4 model-specific rollback method was verified; Sony's update and reinstall paths do not accept older firmware.

warnings: An archived older PUP is not a downgrade method.
Safe Mode reinstall erases console data and does not downgrade.
Any isolated rollback claim needs independent, reproducible confirmation before being treated as usable.

highlights.title: Latest entry exploit
highlights.name: PPPwn
highlights.summary: PPPwn is a PC-driven PPPoE kernel exploit for PS4. It only covers the exact firmware revisions listed and prints PPPwned unless an adapted payload is used.

highlights.title: Latest Linux port
highlights.name: ps4-linux-loader
highlights.summary: PS4 Linux boots a separate Linux kernel via kexec on supported firmware and southbridges. A working entry exploit is still required first.
